questions.q: Which land-use control can the federal government impose?
choices: Zoning rules for a city's downtown
Height limits near airport flight paths
questions.explain: Ottawa can't zone land directly but can regulate where needed for its own powers, like airports and fisheries.

questions.q: A property near farmland has no ALR notation on title, but the ALC's map shows it in the ALR. Which governs?
questions.explain: The ALC's records take precedence. Always check the ALC's ALR map, not just the title.

questions.q: The ALC approves a non-farm use on an ALR parcel. What is the land's status afterwards?
choices: It leaves the ALR completely and for good
It stays in the ALR, subject to the Act
It becomes Crown land held by the ALC
It is rezoned for that use automatically
questions.explain: Only an exclusion removes land from the ALR. Approved non-farm use or subdivision leaves it in.

questions.q: What is the maximum floor area for a newly built principal residence on ALR land?
questions.explain: 500 m² or less, and a local government can set a lower cap.

questions.q: Rezoning land near an intersection with a controlled access highway needs provincial approval within what distance?
questions.explain: 800 metres, under the Transportation Act.

questions.q: Under the Environmental Management Act, when must a site disclosure statement be provided?
choices: On every sale of any property in BC
When seeking approvals for a Schedule 2 site
Only when a buyer asks for one in writing
Whenever a new mortgage is registered
questions.explain: It's triggered by an application for development approval (rezoning, subdivision, permits, demolition, soil removal) on a site with a past Schedule 2 use.

questions.q: What does Mackay v. British Columbia show about heritage sites?
choices: Only designated sites are legally protected
Undesignated sites can still need permits
The province pays all of the heritage costs
Heritage restrictions end on any sale
questions.explain: The Heritage Conservation Act protects undesignated sites too. The buyer faced over $51,000 in heritage reports.

questions.q: Which statute contains the core powers of BC municipalities other than Vancouver?
questions.explain: Since 2004, the Community Charter. The Local Government Act mainly covers regional districts plus planning rules for all.

questions.q: How is a BC municipal council made up?
choices: A mayor and 2 to 4 councillors, 2-year terms
A mayor and 4 to 8 councillors, 4-year terms
questions.explain: An elected mayor plus four to eight councillors, holding office for four years.

questions.q: What power do improvement districts lack?
questions.explain: They provide specific services (water, sewer, fire) and can tax, borrow and expropriate, but have only an advisory role on planning.

questions.q: In an unorganized area with no municipality, who usually acts as the local government?
questions.explain: In unorganized areas, the regional district takes on many municipal roles.

questions.q: Requiring landscaping around parking lots serves which planning goal?
choices: Public health and safety of residents
questions.explain: It's about appearance and convenience, one of the four goals of planning controls.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Why local governments regulate land

questions.q: Who usually makes the final decision to adopt a planning bylaw?
questions.explain: Planners advise, the public is consulted, and elected officials decide.

questions.q: Must every BC municipality adopt an official community plan?
questions.explain: OCPs are optional, though most urban areas have one.

questions.q: An OCP designates land as agricultural. Council wants to rezone it for houses. What must happen first?
questions.explain: Bylaws must be consistent with the OCP, so the OCP must be amended first.

questions.q: What does adopting an OCP commit the local government to?
choices: Building every project shown in the plan
Rezoning all land to match within a year
Compensating owners whose land loses value
questions.explain: An OCP doesn't commit the government to any project, and it isn't a zoning bylaw.

questions.q: OCP housing policies must address anticipated housing needs over at least what period?
questions.explain: At least five years. OCPs generally must be updated every five years.

questions.q: What does a rural land use bylaw combine?
questions.explain: It combines OCP-type policy and zoning in one simpler, cheaper bylaw, with the same effect.

questions.q: How does a zoning bylaw differ from an OCP?
choices: Zoning covers future land use only
Zoning regulates current use in detail
Zoning is optional; OCPs are mandatory
questions.explain: Zoning regulates current use and buildings in detail. The OCP sets current and future policy.

questions.q: A 1,200 m² lot has a floor space ratio of 0.6. What total floor area can be built?
questions.explain: 1,200 × 0.6 = 720 m², whatever the number of storeys.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · What zoning bylaws usually control

questions.q: What is a CD zone?
choices: A commercial district for downtown cores
questions.explain: Comprehensive Development zones are tailored to a particular parcel or parcels.

questions.q: A coach house is strata titled, separate from the main house. Can it be sold separately?
choices: No, never, as it shares the land
Yes, as it's a separate strata lot
Only with a development variance permit
Only after it is 10 years old
questions.explain: The legal structure decides. A strata-titled coach house can be sold separately; a laneway home on the same lot can't.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · What zoning bylaws usually control

questions.q: A listing has an unauthorized suite. What should the listing licensee do?
choices: Advertise it as a handy mortgage helper
Disclose it; don't promote suite income
Say nothing about it unless asked
Have the seller remove it before listing
questions.explain: Promoting it as income breaches Rules s.41; missing permits are a material latent defect that must be disclosed (s.59).
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Secondary suites and short-term rentals

questions.q: Under the 2023 Short-Term Rental Accommodations Act, where can short-term rentals generally operate?
choices: Anywhere the owner chooses to operate
Host's home plus one suite or ADU
Only in licensed hotels and motels
questions.explain: The principal residence requirement limits them to the host's home plus one secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Secondary suites and short-term rentals

questions.q: Can a municipality be stricter than STRAA on short-term rentals?
questions.explain: STRAA is a floor. Municipalities and stratas can impose tighter restrictions (e.g. Vancouver).
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Secondary suites and short-term rentals

questions.q: In the Whistler rental pool case, why was the zoning bylaw upheld?
choices: Zoning bylaws can never be challenged in court
It had a land-use purpose, not discriminatory
The owners had agreed to it in writing
The province had approved it in advance
questions.explain: The court found a valid land-use rationale and no unreasonable discrimination, so regulating users was acceptable.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Secondary suites and short-term rentals

questions.q: How many times must council vote on a rezoning bylaw?
choices: Twice, before and after the hearing
Only once, at the public hearing
questions.explain: Three readings plus final adoption: four separate votes.

questions.q: When is a public hearing generally prohibited for a rezoning?
choices: Residential projects consistent with the OCP
For any project of more than four storeys
For any project once first reading passes
questions.explain: Residential projects consistent with the OCP generally don't get a public hearing, though notice is still given.

questions.q: Council rezones a client's commercial lot to single-family residential, cutting its value. Can the owner claim compensation?
choices: Yes, but only half the loss
Only through the board of variance
questions.explain: The Local Government Act says local governments aren't liable for passing, amending or repealing zoning bylaws or OCPs.

questions.q: What happened to land use contracts in BC?
questions.explain: A 2014 amendment terminated them all by June 30, 2024, without compensation.

questions.q: A lawful non-conforming use stops. How long until it loses its status (outside Vancouver)?
questions.explain: Six continuous months (90 days in Vancouver).

questions.q: A non-conforming building is damaged to 80% of its value. What happens?
choices: It can be rebuilt exactly as before
It must be rebuilt to current rules
questions.explain: Damage of 75% or more of its value means it can only be rebuilt in conformity with the current bylaw.

questions.q: What happens to a non-conforming use when the property is sold?
choices: It continues with the new owner
It continues for one year only
questions.explain: Status continues through changes of ownership.

questions.q: Can a lawful non-conforming use be extended?
choices: Onto adjoining land the owner buys
Anywhere if the owner pays a fee
questions.explain: It can spread through an existing building but not onto a larger area of land.

questions.q: What can a board of variance vary?
choices: Permitted uses in a particular zone
Siting, size and dimensions, if minor
Density limits in any zone it chooses
questions.explain: Only minor variances to zoning rules on siting, size and dimensions, where compliance would cause undue hardship.

questions.q: Which local governments must have a board of variance?
choices: Every one that has adopted zoning
Only regional districts with an OCP
questions.explain: Every local government with a zoning bylaw must establish one.

questions.q: What must exist before a local government can require a development permit?
choices: A rezoning application from the owner
A DP area designated in the OCP
An order from the board of variance
A heritage designation on the title
questions.explain: The area must first be designated as a development permit area in the OCP.

questions.q: A title shows "MAY BE AFFECTED BY A PERMIT UNDER PART 14 OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT ACT". What should you do?
choices: Get the permit from the local government
Ask the land title office for details
questions.explain: The notation gives no details. Get a copy of the permit, especially if any change or development is planned.

questions.q: What can a development variance permit NOT vary?
questions.explain: A DVP can vary many bylaw provisions, but never use or density.

questions.q: How many times can a temporary use permit be renewed?
questions.explain: Only once. Terms are typically up to three years.

questions.q: Who approves subdivision plans in a municipality?
choices: The land title registrar for the area
The approving officer named by council
The board of variance for the area
questions.explain: The approving officer, usually the municipal engineer or planner.

questions.q: A subdivision meets all zoning rules but is refused as against the public interest. When can a court overturn this?
choices: Whenever the plan meets all the zoning rules
Bad faith, discrimination or specious basis
If the owner pays the application fees
If the neighbours all support the plan
questions.explain: Hlynsky: courts interfere only for bad faith, intent to discriminate, or a specious and totally inadequate factual basis.

questions.q: Up to what share of land can a subdivider be required to dedicate for parks?
questions.explain: Up to five percent.

questions.q: How do community amenity contributions differ from DCCs?
choices: CACs are set by bylaw; DCCs are negotiated
CACs are negotiated; DCCs are set by bylaw
questions.explain: DCCs are calculated under a bylaw. CACs must be negotiated and can't be imposed unilaterally.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Development cost charges and amenity contributions

questions.q: An application for a building permit fully complies with the bylaw. Can it be refused?
questions.explain: If the proposed work complies, the building permit must be issued.

questions.q: What does a Community Charter section 57 notice on title indicate?
choices: A heritage designation by the city
A development permit on the land
questions.explain: It warns of a contravention of the building code or a bylaw. Get details from the municipality and recommend legal advice.

questions.q: A buyer confirms the zoning allows a pet store, buys, then is refused a business licence. What check was missed?
choices: The OCP land use designation map
An order of the board of variance
questions.explain: Zoning isn't enough: licensing bylaws can restrict a business the zoning allows.

questions.q: A client asks whether GST applies to their sale. What does Rules s.30(d) require?
choices: Answer based on your own past experience
Advise them to get independent tax advice
Tell them GST never applies to homes
Calculate the GST owing for them
questions.explain: Licensees must advise clients to get independent professional advice on matters outside their expertise.

questions.q: Under the Excise Tax Act, what is the default position for a real property sale?
questions.explain: Every supply is taxable unless an exemption in Schedule V applies.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · The basic rule: taxable unless exempt

questions.q: Which interest in real property can attract GST?
choices: Only a sale of the fee simple estate
Any interest, even an option to buy
Only a lease longer than 99 years
questions.explain: GST potentially applies to any right in real property, including options.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · The basic rule: taxable unless exempt

questions.q: A seller fails to collect GST that was owed on a taxable sale. Who is liable to the CRA?
choices: No one, if the deal closed
questions.explain: The buyer must pay, but a seller who fails to collect is equally liable; the CRA usually assesses the seller.

questions.q: When does a buyer self-assess GST instead of paying it to the seller?
choices: Whenever the price is over $1 million
Whenever the seller agrees to it in the contract
Only on newly built homes from a builder
questions.explain: A GST-registered buyer self-assesses, except an individual buying a residential complex. Also when the seller is a non-resident.

questions.q: When is GST payable on a deposit for a new home?
choices: As soon as the deposit is paid in trust
When it becomes the seller's, at closing
Within 30 days after it is paid
questions.explain: GST generally applies to the deposit once it becomes the seller's money, usually at completion.

questions.q: A doctor buys a building for a clinic (exempt) and leases part to a pharmacy (taxable). What GST can they recover?
choices: All of the GST paid on the building
Only the part for the pharmacy lease
None of it, since a clinic is exempt
Half of it, as required by law
questions.explain: Input tax credits are allowed only to the extent the property is used in commercial (taxable) activities.

questions.q: How long does a taxpayer have to object to a CRA GST assessment?
questions.explain: Ninety days to file an objection; then 90 days to appeal to the Tax Court after confirmation.

questions.q: A house is used mainly for Airbnb stays. How is it likely treated for GST?
choices: As exempt farm land under Schedule V
As an exempt long-term residential rental
questions.explain: Short-term rental homes can fall under the hotel exclusion and be taxable, regardless of age.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Residential complexes and the hotel exclusion

questions.q: What does the GST exemption for resale homes actually depend on?
choices: The home being over 5 years old
The seller not being a builder
The buyer being a first-time buyer
questions.explain: There's no 'used home' exemption as such. The exemption is for sales by someone who isn't a builder.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Builders and the self-supply rule

questions.q: A builder rents a new home to a long-term tenant before selling it. When is GST owed?
questions.explain: The self-supply rule deems a sale to the builder when the tenant moves in; the later sale is exempt.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Builders and the self-supply rule

questions.q: Mr. Jones buys a new home to live in, but is transferred before moving in and sells. Is he a builder?
choices: Yes, because no one had lived there yet
No, he had no business or profit motive
Yes, because he sold it within a year
Only if he made a profit on the sale
questions.explain: An individual must be acting in a business or adventure in the nature of trade to be a builder.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Builders and the self-supply rule

questions.q: Under the standard BC Contract of Purchase and Sale since November 2024, how is GST treated?
choices: It is always extra, on top of the price
It's included in the price, if it applies
It's split equally by buyer and seller
It's left out of the contract entirely
questions.explain: Clause 1 now says the price includes applicable GST, unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Is GST included in the price?

questions.q: For a mixed-use resort condo, which nights count as commercial use for GST?
questions.explain: The CRA counts only nights actually rented, not nights merely listed.

questions.q: Who pays property transfer tax?
questions.explain: The buyer pays it before the transfer can be registered. The seller has no collection role.

questions.q: What is PTT on a $1,500,000 house?
What is PTT on a $3,000,000 home?
What is PTT on a $4,000,000 commercial building?
questions.explain: $2,000 + $36,000 + 3% × $2,000,000 = $98,000. The residential surcharge doesn't apply.

questions.q: Why did PTT on the Zellstoff Celgar pulp mill rise to $4.5 million?
choices: GST was added to the price
questions.explain: Fixtures are part of the land's value for PTT, so classifying the equipment as fixtures raised the tax dramatically.

questions.q: PTT on an assigned presale strata unit is based on what?
choices: Market value of the unit at closing
The unit's assessed value that year
questions.explain: For presale strata units, PTT is on the price plus amounts paid to assignors and the developer, not value at closing.

questions.q: Which buyer qualifies for the First Time Home Buyers' exemption?
choices: A PR who once owned a home in Europe years ago
A citizen in BC 1 year buying an $800K home
A citizen buying an $850K rental condo
A foreign student buying a small condo
questions.explain: Must be a citizen or PR, generally in BC a year, never owned a principal residence anywhere, and FMV ≤ $835,000 as a principal residence.

questions.q: Under the First Time Home Buyers' Program, PTT is exempt on what portion of the price?
questions.explain: The first $500,000, for homes up to $835,000 (partial relief up to $860,000).

questions.q: What is the full-exemption threshold for the Newly Built Home Exemption?
questions.explain: Fair market value of $1,100,000 or less, with partial relief up to $1,150,000.

questions.q: What is the rate of the additional PTT for foreign buyers?
questions.explain: 20% since February 21, 2018 (it started at 15% in 2016).

questions.q: Two buyers purchase a Metro Vancouver home together; one is a foreign national. How much of the purchase may attract the foreign buyers' tax?
questions.explain: There's no split for multiple buyers. If one is foreign, the whole purchase may be taxed.

questions.q: Is a BC-incorporated company always outside the foreign corporation definition?
choices: Yes, if it's incorporated in BC
No, foreign control can make it foreign
Yes, if it has its head office in BC
Yes, if it files and pays BC taxes
questions.explain: A corporation controlled by foreign nationals is a foreign corporation even if incorporated in Canada.

questions.q: In Shave v. Century 21, what was the licensee's main failing?
choices: Charging the buyers too much commission
Missing the date for removing subjects
Failing to arrange a home inspection
questions.explain: The licensee changed the declaration to 'yes' without confirming it and didn't flag it, and was 75% liable for about $175,000.

questions.q: A non-resident sells a rental building with no clearance certificate. What must the buyer withhold?
questions.explain: 50% of the gross price for depreciable property; 25% for non-depreciable property like a residence.

questions.q: How can a buyer protect themselves from liability for a non-resident seller's tax?
choices: By paying a much larger deposit
By a reasonable inquiry into residency
By taking title through a bare trust
By closing the deal as fast as possible
questions.explain: Income Tax Act s.116(5): a reasonable inquiry protects the buyer. In Mao v. Liu, the notary didn't, and was liable.

questions.q: A $400,000 profit is treated as business income rather than a capital gain. How much is taxable?
questions.explain: Business income is 100% taxable; only 50% of a capital gain is.

questions.q: In Happy Valley Farms, which factor usually carries the most weight?
questions.explain: Motive generally has the greatest influence, including any secondary intention to resell for profit.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · Is it income or capital?

questions.q: Under the federal flipping rule, a home held for under what period is deemed business income?
questions.explain: Under 365 days, unless a life-event exception applies. The principal residence exemption isn't available.

questions.q: What is the BC home flipping tax rate on a gain if sold within 365 days?
questions.explain: 20%, declining to zero by 730 days. It's filed separately within 90 days of the sale.

questions.q: Does the BC home flipping tax apply to BC residents?
choices: No, it applies only to non-residents
Yes, to anyone selling BC property
Only to foreign nationals and companies
questions.explain: It applies to any individual or entity, regardless of residency.

questions.q: A property's net taxable value is $600,000 and the mill rate is 3.5. What is the tax?
Who is liable for property tax under the Assessment Act?
choices: Whoever is living in the property
The registered owner, incl. a life tenant
The lender holding the first mortgage
The brokerage that last listed it
questions.explain: The registered owner (including a life tenant or agreement for sale holder) as of November 30.

questions.q: Which is NOT an improvement for property assessment?
questions.explain: Production machinery, things moved as a unit and easily moved furniture are excluded unless they're a building.

questions.q: What is the valuation date for the annual assessment roll?
questions.explain: July 1, with physical condition and permitted use taken as of October 31.

questions.q: Which property class covers offices and stores?
questions.explain: Class 6: Business and Other. Class 1 is residential; Class 5 is light industry.

questions.q: How is a building with ground-floor shops and apartments above classified?
questions.explain: The assessor divides the value between classes: a split classification.

questions.q: What additional school tax applies to a $3,500,000 residential property?
questions.explain: 0.2% on the $500,000 above $3 million = $1,000.

questions.q: A sale is registered on December 15. Whose name appears on that year's assessment roll?
questions.explain: The roll uses land title records as of November 30, so the seller still appears.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · The assessment and tax calendar

questions.q: What is the deadline to file an assessment complaint with the assessor?
questions.explain: January 31. Review panels then sit February 1 to March 15.

questions.q: After a review panel decision, where does an owner appeal next, and by when?
choices: Tax Court of Canada within 90 days
questions.explain: To the Property Assessment Appeal Board by April 30; further appeals on points of law go to the courts.

questions.q: An owner thinks their tax bill is too high. What can they appeal?
questions.explain: Owners appeal the assessment, not the tax itself.

questions.q: Why shouldn't a licensee rely on assessed value as market value?
choices: It reflects a past date, July 1
It's always set too high on purpose
It leaves out the value of the land
questions.explain: It's a July 1 snapshot, often outdated by the time it's mailed. Dosanjh v. Liang refused to treat it as evidence of value.
questions.ref: Lesson 14 · The assessment and tax calendar

questions.q: Which owner can ask to be assessed on current residential use instead of a higher zoned use?
choices: Any owner who applies in writing
A 10+ year resident on up-zoned land
A new buyer of a development site
A landlord who owns a rental building
questions.explain: The resident-owner must have lived there continuously for 10 years, apply each year, and the land must be zoned or influenced for a higher use.

questions.q: What is the basic home owner grant in Metro Vancouver?
questions.explain: $570 in Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley and the Capital Regional District; $770 in northern and rural areas.

questions.q: What minimum equity is required for the regular property tax deferment program?
questions.explain: 25% for the regular program (55+, surviving spouse or disability); 15% for the families with children program.

questions.q: A seller has deferred property taxes. When must they be repaid?
choices: Never; deferred taxes are forgiven over time
Before the property is sold or transferred
Only when the owner eventually dies
Within 30 days of each tax due date
questions.explain: The deferral is a registered charge that must be repaid before a sale or transfer can be registered.

questions.q: What is the 2026 SVT rate for a Canadian citizen who isn't in a satellite family?
questions.explain: 1% for Canadians and PRs; 3% for foreign owners and satellite families.

questions.q: An owner in a taxable area doesn't file an SVT declaration. What happens?
choices: They're taxed at the highest rate
They lose the home owner grant
questions.explain: Every owner must declare by March 31, even if exempt. Non-filers are charged the maximum rate.

questions.q: To qualify for the SVT rental exemption, how long must the property be rented?
choices: 3 months in total, in any periods
12 months in a row, with one tenant
30 days in a row at any time of year
questions.explain: At least six months of the year, in increments of a month or longer.

questions.q: When is someone part of a satellite family for SVT purposes?
choices: When they live outside BC most of the year
Unreported income tops income reported here
When they own two or more homes in BC
When they are not a Canadian citizen
questions.explain: It compares worldwide unreported income with income reported in Canada (spouses combined), so even citizens can be caught.

questions.q: What is the City of Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax rate?
questions.explain: 3% of the taxable assessed value for homes vacant six months or more.

questions.q: An investor rents a Vancouver condo only on stays of under 30 days. How is it treated for the EHT?
choices: As occupied, since it was rented
As vacant, so subject to the tax
questions.explain: Only rentals of at least 30 consecutive days count toward the six months of occupancy.

questions.q: What happens if an owner doesn't file a Property Status Declaration?
questions.explain: No PSD means the property is deemed vacant and taxed. False declarations can be fined up to $10,000.

questions.q: Who is generally exempt from filing under the federal Underused Housing Tax?
choices: Foreign nationals holding a work permit
Any owner of a recreational vacation home
questions.explain: Citizens and PRs are excluded owners (unless they hold as partners or trustees). Private corporations generally must file.

questions.q: An affected owner qualifies for a UHT exemption. Must they still file?
choices: No, an exemption removes the need to file
Yes, by April 30, or face penalties
Only if the home sat vacant all year
questions.explain: Affected owners must file even when exempt. Minimum penalties are $1,000 (individual) or $2,000 (corporation).
